standard_prerequisites.name: Induction on the degree of a finite field extension
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the start of the counted proof (lines 44902-44908)
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces to the case where the extension is generated by a single element, by splitting off an intermediate field.

standard_prerequisites.name: The minimal polynomial of a primitive element
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the monic relation whose coefficients are realised in R and then used to define S.

core_obligations: Induct on the degree: settle degree one by taking S equal to R, and reduce to a primitive extension when an intermediate field exists (proof lines 44902-44908).

For a primitive extension take the minimal polynomial of a generator and realise its coefficients as images of elements of R, first allowing a common denominator g outside the prime and then absorbing g by rescaling the generator (proof lines 44910-44916).
Take S to be R adjoined a root of that polynomial and read off that the extension of residue fields is the prescribed one (proof lines 44916-44917).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the primitive case by induction on the degree (proof lines 44901-44909).
Realise the coefficients of the minimal polynomial in R and adjoin a root (proof lines 44910-44918).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a prime p of a ring R and a finite field extension L of the residue field at p, there is a finite free ring map R to S such that pS is prime with residue field extension isomorphic to the prescribed one (statement lines 44891-44899). The proof does not appeal to a structure theorem for finite free extensions: it inducts on the degree, reduces to an extension generated by one element, writes the coefficients of its minimal polynomial as images of elements of R after clearing a denominator outside p, absorbs that denominator by rescaling the generator, and then adjoins a root of the resulting monic polynomial (proof lines 44901-44918). The clearing and the rescaling of the generator are the steps that make the construction work. H2.
